scope: Bounded real-literature evidence audit for Agent/RAG long-context evidence ordering; no model benchmark run

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.locator: MIT Press full text §§2.3, 5 and Conclusion
papers.can_support: In the tasks and models examined, the position of answer-bearing content changes performance, often with worse performance in the middle.
papers.cannot_support: All modern models or all deployed RAG systems are dominated by positional bias.

papers.title: Found in the middle: Calibrating Positional Attention Bias Improves Long Context Utilization
papers.can_support: The authors report attention-bias calibration with improved relevant-information access and RAG performance in evaluated settings.
papers.cannot_support: Position bias has been eliminated from every model, task, and production RAG setting.

papers.title: Mitigate Position Bias in LLMs via Scaling a Single Hidden States Channel
papers.can_support: The authors report mitigating positional bias by intervening on a hidden-state channel on several evaluated benchmarks and models.
papers.cannot_support: Every instance of positional bias is entirely solved or this method is best under matched latency/compute budgets.

papers.title: Do RAG Systems Really Suffer From Positional Bias?
papers.can_support: The authors find positional bias has marginal impact in their tested realistic retrieval pipelines because distracting and relevant passages are both affected.
papers.cannot_support: All RAG applications have negligible positional bias, or the original controlled experiments were invalid.

papers.title: Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval
papers.can_support: In studied models and tasks, long inputs can hurt performance even when relevant evidence is perfectly retrieved.
papers.cannot_support: Position bias alone explains all long-context quality problems.

claims.text: In Liu et al.'s controlled tasks, placing relevant evidence in the middle can degrade answer accuracy.
No later research has proposed or tested mitigations for the lost-in-the-middle effect.
Position bias is always the dominant source of errors in deployed RAG systems.
Once retrieval is perfect, extra context length cannot hurt the language model.
A new joint uncertainty-aware routing and context-position method is already validated and novel.

gaps.unresolved_part: Which effects and interventions transport across controlled versus realistic RAG pipelines is context-specific and requires targeted data and comparisons.
gaps.reason: Published mitigations exist, and later deployment-oriented evaluation complicates any universal causal claim.
